channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: US President Trump Calls Iranian Leadership 'Crazy People,' Rejects Truce Offer
item.description: U.S. President Donald Trump described Iran's leadership as 'crazy people' and officially rejected a proposed truce from Tehran. Trump has consistently used harsh rhetoric against Iranian authorities. This follows a previous report where Trump rejected Iran's offer for a seven-day ceasefire.

item.title: Ashgabat Hosts Turkmenistan Investment Forum with Over 800 Participants
item.description: Turkmenistan is hosting an investment forum in Ashgabat on October 1-2, expecting over 800 participants from numerous countries. The event, organized by the finance and foreign ministries, aims to showcase the country's economic potential, including its natural gas reserves and diversifying economy. Discussions will cover export routes, transit corridors, and public-private partnerships.

item.title: Fifth Samarkand Forum on Human Rights Focuses on Effective Implementation
item.description: The Fifth Samarkand Forum on Human Rights is underway in Tashkent, focusing on implementing international human rights obligations and marking the 30th anniversary of Uzbekistan's National Center for Human Rights. High-level participants discussed the role of national mechanisms in human rights implementation, with speakers including judicial and parliamentary leaders from Uzbekistan and international rights officials.

item.title: Taliban Justice Ministry Closes Shiite Institutions in Western Kabul
item.description: Local sources reported that the Taliban's justice ministry has closed three institutions serving the Shiite community in western Kabul. These include Al-Zahra Clinic, the Tebyan Center, and the Resalat religious school. The ministry reportedly provided no clear reason for the closures, continuing a pattern of targeting Shiite-linked organizations.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Calls for Issyk-Kul Preservation Fund at UN
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov urged the creation of a fund to preserve Lake Issyk-Kul during his UN General Assembly address. He also highlighted Kyrgyzstan's election to the UN Security Council for 2027-2028, emphasizing the responsibility and Central Asia's growing role. Japarov advocated for Security Council expansion.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Defense Minister dismissed after Caspian Sea military exercise tragedy
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev dismissed Defense Minister Dauren Kosanov three days after a tragic incident during naval exercises on the Caspian Sea coast resulted in the deaths of fourteen servicemen. An investigation is underway, and several officers have been arrested.

item.title: Rogun Dam project advances with World Bank funding despite past doubts
item.description: Construction on Tajikistan's Rogun Dam project has progressed significantly, with the World Bank approving a $300 million grant, its second round of funding. WeBuild Group began work on Lot 2 and raised the dam's height, increasing reservoir water levels and generation capacity.

item.title: Chinese investors to inject up to $500 million into three wind farms in Akmola region
item.description: Chinese investors have signed agreements to build three wind power stations and modernize an elevator in Kazakhstan's Akmola region. The total investment for these projects could reach $506 million. The wind farms, with a combined capacity of 450 MW, are planned for construction starting in October 2026 and completion by 2028.

item.title: Afghanistan Journalists Center reports increased censorship and pressure on media
item.description: The Afghanistan Journalists Center (AFJC) states that media and journalists face growing restrictions, including pre-publication censorship, protest coverage bans, and pressure for content approval. Restrictions on women journalists have increased, and some international TV broadcasts are banned. The AFJC urges the Taliban to revoke restrictive orders.

item.title: UN allocates over $1.7 million to support women entrepreneurs in Afghanistan
item.description: UN Women will provide $1.7 million to support approximately 1,500 Afghan women entrepreneurs over the next year through a joint initiative with the UNDP. The program includes financial support, business development services, literacy training, and market access assistance, indirectly benefiting over 14,000 people.

item.title: Kazakhstan-China border crossings to close for three days due to PRC National Day
item.description: Vehicle checkpoints on the Kazakhstan-China border will be closed from October 1 to 3 for the People's Republic of China's National Day. The State Revenue Committee of Kazakhstan's Ministry of Finance announced that railway checkpoints will continue to operate normally. Travelers are advised to be aware of these temporary restrictions.

item.title: UN General Assembly confronts global crises amid power politics overshadowing shared needs
item.description: The 81st UN General Assembly convenes amidst simultaneous global crises including wars, displacement, poverty, and climate change. Geopolitical rivalry and national interests dominate discourse, widening the gap between global problems and national responses, potentially weakening international order and law enforcement.

item.title: Girls in Afghanistan face hardship and health risks due to early marriage after education ban
item.description: Girls in Afghanistan, forced into early marriage after the Taliban banned education beyond sixth grade, describe hardships and lack of understanding of marital responsibilities. Obstetricians warn of increased health risks for adolescent mothers and their babies due to premature pregnancy and childbirth.

item.title: Kazakhstan Proposes Making Roads Profitable for Neighboring Countries
item.description: Kazakhstan aims to develop its road and rail networks to generate revenue for neighboring countries as well. Deputy Prime Minister Serik Zhumangarin discussed financing mechanisms with a World Bank representative. The goal is to create a unified Central Asian infrastructure chain, making transit routes profitable for all involved.

item.title: Uzbekistan Strengthens Child Protection Laws, Increasing Liability Measures
item.description: Uzbekistan is taking a significant step to protect children from violence by strengthening liability measures. A draft law addressing this issue is scheduled for review at the lower house's next session on September 29. This initiative aims to enhance child protection mechanisms within the country.

item.title: Uzbekistan plans to enroll 80% of third and fourth-year students in dual education
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to enroll at least 80% of its third and fourth-year university students, approximately 185,000, in dual education programs. This initiative aims to adapt Germany's successful dual education model, where graduates often continue working at their internship companies. The program will prioritize engineering, manufacturing, construction, and agriculture.

item.title: Ashgabat Military Parade Showcases New Air Defense Systems on Independence Day
item.description: Ashgabat hosted a military parade celebrating the 35th anniversary of Turkmenistan's independence. The event featured a display of the country's military hardware, including newly acquired air defense systems. Daryo.uz highlighted the most significant equipment presented during the parade.

item.title: Kazakh President Orders Military Reforms After 14 Soldiers Die in Exercise
item.description: Following the deaths of 14 soldiers during exercises in the Mangystau region, Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has ordered a comprehensive reform of the armed forces. He stated the army is "stuck in the last century" and requires modernization based on international best practices.

item.title: Almaty Unveils Project to Reduce Private Car Use by 20% by 2040
item.description: Almaty plans to reduce private car usage by 20% by 2040, aiming to increase public transport trips to 2.3 million by 2030. The city will develop metro, light rail, and SkyTrain systems, and build logistics hubs. The Kalkaman metro station is set to open by year-end, extending to the "Baryk" hub.

item.title: Kazakhstan-China Border Vehicle Checkpoints to Close for Three Days
item.description: Vehicle checkpoints on the Kazakhstan-China border will be closed from October 1 to 3 due to the celebration of the PRC's National Day. The State Revenue Committee of Kazakhstan announced that the passage of people, vehicles, and cargo will be suspended. Railway checkpoints will continue to operate normally. Carriers are advised to plan accordingly.

item.title: Afghanistan Journalists Center: Taliban Systematically Restrict Access to Information
item.description: The Afghanistan Journalists Center (AJC) reports that the Taliban have systematically restricted public access to information, effectively eliminating this right. Since August 2021, at least 24 directives have been issued that conflict with Afghan media and access to information laws, further constraining journalists' activities and people's access to necessary information.

item.title: Osh Construction Company Blacklisted for Violations, Ordered to Restore Site
item.description: The Ministry of Construction in Kyrgyzstan has ordered the construction company "Altyn Stroy Group" in Osh to fully restore a damaged site within a week. The company was previously fined and had its license suspended for operating without permits and damaging a sidewalk. Disciplinary action was taken against local construction control officials.

item.title: Labor Rights to Be Monitored During Uzbekistan's Cotton Harvest Season
item.description: Labor rights will be monitored during Uzbekistan's cotton harvest. Parents are urged to create conditions for their children's education and prevent their involvement in cotton picking. This measure aims to ensure fair labor practices and protect children's right to education.

item.title: Herat-Khaf Railway's Fourth Section First Phase Inaugurated
item.description: The first phase of the fourth section of the Herat-Khaf railway, spanning 43 kilometers and costing over $57 million, has been completed and inaugurated. The project was built in cooperation with a Kazakh company, facilitating faster and more cost-effective goods transportation.

item.title: Student Dormitories to Be Built in Three Major Southern Kyrgyz Cities
item.description: Student dormitories are planned for construction in Osh, Manas, and Batken as part of a working trip by Nurdana Oruntaev. The Ministry of Construction announced the initiative to address student housing needs in these major southern cities of Kyrgyzstan.

item.title: Individuals Deleted Posts Criticizing Caspian Sea Incident After Police Contact
item.description: Following the deaths of 14 soldiers in a Caspian Sea incident, some social media users reported deleting critical posts after being contacted by police. An expert believes such actions undermine public trust in authorities. One individual was asked by police to remove a post demanding a trial for former officials.

item.title: New Defense Minister Outlines Reforms for Kazakhstan's Armed Forces
item.description: Kazakhstan's new Defense Minister, Aidoss Mirzakhmetov, held his first meeting with the leadership, detailing key tasks for reforming the armed forces. Priorities include enhancing combat readiness, improving the command system, and developing weaponry and military equipment.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Arrives in Berlin for Talks
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has arrived in Berlin for important negotiations with German leadership. He is also scheduled to visit Munich and meet with executives from leading German companies, financial, and scientific institutions.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev begins official visit to Germany
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has arrived in Germany for an official visit at the invitation of Federal President Frank-Walter Steinmeier. Discussions in Berlin will focus on strengthening strategic partnership between Kazakhstan and Germany. Tokayev will also visit Munich and meet with business leaders and academics.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev arrives in Germany for talks with Steinmeier and Merz
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has arrived in Berlin for an official visit to Germany. He will hold talks with Federal President Frank-Walter Steinmeier and Chancellor Friedrich Merz to discuss strengthening the strategic partnership between Kazakhstan and Germany. Tokayev will also visit Munich and meet with German business and financial leaders.

item.title: Talks and business forums: Tokayev arrives on a visit to Germany
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has arrived in Germany for an official visit at the invitation of Federal President Frank-Walter Steinmeier. In Berlin, Tokayev will hold talks with Steinmeier and Federal Chancellor Friedrich Merz to discuss strengthening the strategic partnership between Kazakhstan and Germany. He will also visit Munich and participate in business forums.

item.title: Kassym-Jomart Tokayev arrives in Germany for an official visit
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has arrived in Germany for an official visit at the invitation of Federal President Frank-Walter Steinmeier. In Berlin, Tokayev is scheduled to hold talks with German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier and Federal Chancellor Friedrich Merz to discuss strengthening the strategic partnership between Kazakhstan and Germany. He will also visit Munich.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Central Election Commission Reports No Presidential Candidacy Applications Yet
item.description: The Central Commission for Elections and Referendums in Kyrgyzstan has not yet received any applications from individuals intending to participate in the upcoming presidential elections. The commission awaits formal declarations of intent from potential candidates.

item.title: Kazakh Businesses Urge Reversal of Ban on Deductions for Simplified Tax Regime
item.description: Kazakh businesses are again requesting the cancellation of the ban on deductions for transactions with entities under the simplified tax regime. The National Chamber of Entrepreneurs "Atameken" is involved in discussions regarding proposed amendments to the Tax Code.

item.title: Bishkek Vocational Lyceum Graduate Awarded at WorldSkills Shanghai
item.description: Hanifa Syrgakova, a graduate of Vocational Lyceum No. 18 in Bishkek, received the Best of Nation award at the WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 championship. She competed in "Fashion Technology" and achieved the best result among Kyrgyzstan's national team. Kyrgyzstan officially joined the WorldSkills movement in 2023.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Host UN Crime Prevention Congress in 2031
item.description: Uzbekistan will host the 16th UN Congress on Crime Prevention and Criminal Justice in 2031. The decision was announced by Head of the Presidential Administration Saida Mirziyoyeva at the 15th Congress in Abu Dhabi. This signifies international trust in Uzbekistan's openness and readiness for cooperation.

item.title: Tokayev Replaces Defense Minister After Soldiers' Deaths, Orders Army Reform
item.description: Following the deaths of soldiers, Kazakhstan's President Tokayev has replaced the Defense Minister and ordered a reform of the army. Police have contacted individuals who criticized the authorities online after the military personnel's deaths. An earthquake was also felt in Almaty today.

item.title: Flooding in Thailand Causes $320 Million in Economic Damage
item.description: Ongoing heavy rains in Thailand have caused widespread flooding, displacing thousands of people to safer areas. Much of the capital, Bangkok, is submerged, with "floating" market stalls appearing. The floods have resulted in an estimated $320 million in economic damage.

item.title: Critics Delete Posts After Caspian Sea Incident, Experts Cite Government Miscommunication
item.description: Following the deaths of 14 soldiers in a Caspian Sea incident, several individuals who posted critical comments online have reportedly deleted them after police contact. Experts suggest the authorities mishandled communication with the public and attempted to suppress criticism through pressure.

item.title: Olympic Judo Champion Diera Keldiyeva to Return to Competition in Kazakhstan
item.description: Olympic judo champion Diera Keldiyeva of Uzbekistan will return to competition after a two-year break and childbirth. She has applied to compete in the Open European Cup in Aktau, Kazakhstan, in the 52kg category, her first official competition since the Paris Olympics.
